UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the app, linking to their associated team. This entity stores application-specific user data, separate from authentication details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: The public username chosen by the user for display in rankings and other UI elements.

teamId.description: Reference to the Team the user is associated with. (Relationship: Team 1:N UserProfile)

Team.title: Team
Team.description: Represents a football team participating in leagues and cup tournaments within the app.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Team entity.

name.description: The official name of the football team.

logoUrl.description: URL to the team's logo image.

League.title: League
League.description: Represents a league tournament, including its participating teams and schedule.

id.description: Unique identifier for the League entity.

name.description: The name of the league tournament.

startDate.description: The start date and time of the league tournament.

endDate.description: The end date and time of the league tournament.

teamIds.description: References to Teams participating in this league. (Relationship: League N:N Team)

Cup.title: Cup
Cup.description: Represents a cup tournament, including its participating teams, schedule, and current stage.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Cup entity.

name.description: The name of the cup tournament.

startDate.description: The start date and time of the cup tournament.

endDate.description: The end date and time of the cup tournament.

teamIds.description: References to Teams participating in this cup. (Relationship: Cup N:N Team)

currentRound.description: Describes the current stage or round of the cup tournament (e.g., 'Group Stage', 'Quarter-Finals', 'Semi-Finals', 'Final').

Match.title: Match
Match.description: Represents a single match played between two teams, associated with either a league or a cup.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Match entity.

leagueId.description: Reference to the League if this match is part of a league tournament. Either leagueId or cupId must be present. (Relationship: League 1:N Match)

cupId.description: Reference to the Cup if this match is part of a cup tournament. Either leagueId or cupId must be present. (Relationship: Cup 1:N Match)

homeTeamId.description: Reference to the Team playing as the home team. (Relationship: Team N:1 Match)

awayTeamId.description: Reference to the Team playing as the away team. (Relationship: Team N:1 Match)

matchDate.description: The date and time when the match is scheduled or was played.

homeScore.description: The number of goals or points scored by the home team. Can be null if the match is not yet completed.

awayScore.description: The number of goals or points scored by the away team. Can be null if the match is not yet completed.

status.description: The current status of the match (e.g., 'scheduled', 'completed', 'postponed', 'cancelled').

winnerTeamId.description: Reference to the Team that won the match. Null if the match was a draw or not yet completed. (Relationship: Team N:1 Match)

definition.description: Stores individual user profile data. Each document's ID (`userProfileId`) MUST match the Firebase Authentication UID of the owning user, enabling direct, authorization-independent access control. This collection implicitly manages user ownership.

This collection is top-level to support global queries and uniform security (public read, admin write), ensuring authorization independence from parent tournaments. definition.description: A collection used for Database Access Control (DBAC). The mere existence of a document where `adminId` matches `request.auth.uid` grants global administrative privileges for managing game data (teams, leagues, cups, matches). Documents can be empty or contain minimal role-related data.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique identifier of a user who has administrative privileges, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation.

1.  **Authorization Independence (Denormalization Strategy):**
    *   **User Profiles:** User profiles are stored in `/userProfiles/{userProfileId}` where `userProfileId` is designed to be the Firebase Authentication `uid`. This ensures that access rules for a user's profile (`read` and `write`) can be determined solely by comparing `request.auth.uid` to the document ID, without needing any `get()` operations to check a parent document or user roles. The `UserProfile.id` field is also set to this `uid` for self-contained validation.
    *   **Global Admin Roles:** Administrative write access to the `teams`, `leagues`, `cups`, and `matches` collections is controlled by an `/admins/{adminId}` collection. The presence of a document in this collection (where `adminId` is `request.auth.uid`) grants admin privileges. This is an existence check, which is highly efficient and authorization-independent, avoiding complex `get()` calls in rules.
    *   **Public Data:** All `teams`, `leagues`, `cups`, and `matches` are publicly readable. Their write access is restricted to global admins. This design means that access to a `Match` document, for example, does *not* depend on looking up its parent `League` or `Cup` document. The `leagueId` and `cupId` fields within the `Match` document are for data relationships and querying, not for authorization, thus preserving independence.

2.  **Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
    *   **`/userProfiles/{userProfileId}`:** This collection is segregated for private user data, where each user has exclusive `read/write` access to their own profile.
    *   **`/teams/{teamId}`:** Contains public team information, managed by administrators.
    *   **`/leagues/{leagueId}`:** Contains public league information, managed by administrators.
    *   **`/cups/{cupId}`:** Contains public cup tournament information, managed by administrators.
    *   **`/matches/{matchId}`:** Contains public match data. By placing matches in a top-level collection, we avoid mixing security postures that would arise if they were subcollections of both `leagues` and `cups` (e.g., if league-specific permissions existed). This also simplifies queries across all matches or for matches belonging to a specific league/cup.
    *   **`/admins/{adminId}`:** This dedicated collection strictly defines who has administrative privileges, separating role data from application data.

3.  **Query Ability and Performance (QAPs - Rules are not Filters):**
    *   The structure supports efficient `list` operations (QAPs) because each collection has a uniform security posture:
        *   **User Profiles:** A user can only `list` or `get` their *own* profile. The rule `request.auth.uid == userProfileId` ensures no unauthorized profiles are returned without complex filtering.
        *   **Teams, Leagues, Cups, Matches:** These collections are entirely publicly readable. Therefore, a `list` operation on any of these collections will return all documents without needing any server-side filtering by security rules.
